entries.q: Can I see an actual photo of my plant before it's delivered?
entries.a: Yes. Our catalog photos are taken at our local UAE nursery, and each plant is individual, so small variations occur. Add the note 'Please send plant photo before delivery' at checkout, or message us on WhatsApp with your Order # and we'll send a pre-dispatch photo.

entries.q: I already placed my order. How do I get a photo?
entries.a: Message us on WhatsApp at +971 4 294 1422 with your Order # and ask for a pre-dispatch photo. We'll send you a picture of your plant before it leaves.
entries.note: Pre-dispatch photo service: team to confirm.

entries.q: Will my plant look exactly like the website photo?
entries.a: You'll receive the variety and size you ordered, but every plant grows individually, so leaf count, shape and shade can differ from the photo, which is representative. For peace of mind, ask for a pre-dispatch photo at checkout or on WhatsApp.
entries.original_a: You'll receive the same plant variety from the same nursery. Every plant grows individually, so leaf count, shape and shade can differ slightly from the photo. For peace of mind, request a pre-dispatch photo at checkout or on WhatsApp.
entries.note: Variation part matches Refund policy 3.1. Removed 'from the same nursery' (policy: trusted growers). Pre-dispatch photo: team to confirm.

entries.q: Are your photos real?
entries.a: Yes. Catalog photos are shot at our local UAE nursery. Because each plant is individual, yours may vary a little in fullness or leaf shape. You can request a photo of your own plant before delivery.
entries.note: Policy says photos are representative and plants come from trusted growers; confirm whether catalog photos are shot at your own nursery.

entries.q: Do I get the exact plant in the photo?
entries.a: Photos show our nursery stock, but plants are individual, so you may receive a slightly different plant of the same variety and size. To see yours first, add the note 'Please send plant photo before delivery' at checkout.
entries.note: Variation matches Refund policy 3.1; photo note at checkout needs confirming.

entries.q: How is plant size measured?
entries.a: Size is measured from the bottom of the nursery pot to the top tip of the highest leaf. A plant listed as 50-60 CM stands in that range measured this way.
entries.note: Measuring method is not in any policy; team to confirm.

entries.q: My plant looks a little shorter or taller than the listing. Why?
entries.a: Sizes are ranges because each plant grows naturally; we measure from the base of the nursery pot to the tip of the highest leaf. Small differences from the photo or listing are normal for live plants. If it looks clearly outside the listed range, send a photo with your order number on WhatsApp (+971 4 294 1422) and we'll check.
entries.original_a: Sizes are listed as ranges because each plant grows naturally. We measure from the base of the nursery pot to the tip of the highest leaf. If your plant seems outside the range, send a photo with your Order # on WhatsApp and we'll check.
entries.note: Refund policy 3.1: size differences within normal variation are not grounds for a return. The answer should not suggest otherwise.

entries.q: Which size should I choose?
entries.a: For desks and shelves, 20-40 CM plants suit well. For side tables and consoles, 50-80 CM. For floor corners and statement spots, 100 CM and above. Tell me the space and I'll suggest a size.
entries.note: General sizing advice; no conflict.

entries.q: What pot does a standard order arrive in?
entries.a: Standard orders arrive in sturdy black nursery pots. It's the most economical option, and works well if you plan to repot into your own planter.
entries.note: Pot contents are internal practice; team to confirm.

entries.q: What does a decorative pot order include?
entries.a: Decorative pot selections arrive 100% fully potted. The pot is filled with premium soil mix and perlite, with a drainage layer at the base, so it's ready to display on arrival.
entries.note: Pot contents are internal practice; team to confirm.

entries.q: Which pot option should I choose, nursery or decorative?
entries.a: Choose the nursery pot for the lowest price or if you already have a planter. Choose a decorative pot for a ready-to-display plant that arrives fully potted with soil mix, perlite and a drainage layer. The plant itself is the same.
entries.note: Pot contents are internal practice; team to confirm.

entries.q: Can I change my pot choice after ordering?
entries.a: I'll pass this to our team so they can check whether your order has already been prepared. Please message +971 4 294 1422 with your Order # and the pot you'd prefer.
entries.note: Not covered by policy.

entries.q: Do the decorative pots have drainage holes?
entries.a: Decorative pot orders include a drainage layer at the base, with premium soil mix and perlite. For specific details on a particular pot model, send us the product link and our team will confirm.
entries.note: Whether decorative pots have holes is not in any policy; team to confirm per pot range.

entries.q: Are your plants real or artificial?
entries.a: Our plants are live unless the product says otherwise: artificial items have 'Artificial' or 'Faux' in the product name. If you're unsure about a listing, send me the link.
entries.original_a: Listings titled 'Live' or showing plant care details are real plants. Artificial plants are clearly labelled 'Artificial' in the product title or tags. If you're unsure about a listing, send me the link.
entries.note: Catalog check: 44 artificial products, titled either 'Artificial' or 'Faux'. Nothing is titled 'Live'.

entries.q: Do you have plants taller than 2 metres?
entries.a: Yes, we supply large trees and palms. They are custom orders: our team sends a proposal with the price, delivery fee and timing for your location before the order is confirmed. Share the plant, size and delivery emirate and I'll pass it on.
entries.original_a: Yes, we have large specimen plants. Because they need special handling and delivery planning, our team handles these personally. Please share the plant, size and delivery emirate and I'll pass it on.
entries.note: Shipping policy 7: large trees, palms and bulk orders are custom orders agreed in a proposal.

entries.q: Is the plant healthy on arrival? Can I check first?
entries.a: Plants are guaranteed to arrive healthy. Check your plant with the delivery agent: if it's damaged or not what you ordered, you can refuse it on the spot. If you find damage after unpacking, send photos and your order number on WhatsApp (+971 4 294 1422) or email sales@plantsworld.ae within 24 hours and we'll replace it free. You can also ask for a pre-dispatch photo.

entries.note: Refund policy 3.2–4: inspect with the delivery agent and refuse on the spot, or report within 24 hours; damaged items are replaced free. There is no 'Transit Guarantee' or 'credit' in the policy.

entries.q: How much light do indoor plants need in the UAE?
entries.a: Most indoor plants like bright, indirect light. Avoid direct midday sun through glass, which can scorch leaves. Low-light options such as Snake Plant, ZZ Plant and Pothos cope well in dimmer rooms.
entries.note: Matches guide research and baseline sun-through-glass.

entries.q: How often should I water my plant?
entries.a: Water when the top of the soil feels dry, then let excess drain. Needs vary by plant: succulents like Snake and ZZ need less water than leafy plants. Overwatering is the most common cause of plant problems.
entries.note: Matches guide research (check soil, not calendar).

entries.q: My plant has yellow leaves. What's wrong?
entries.a: Yellow leaves are most often caused by overwatering or poor drainage. Let the soil dry out, check the drainage, and remove yellow leaves. A few yellow leaves after delivery are normal. If it continues, send a photo with the plant name.
entries.original_a: Yellow leaves are most often caused by overwatering or poor drainage. Let the soil dry out, check the drainage, and remove yellow leaves. If it continues, send a photo with the plant name.
entries.note: Added that a few yellow leaves after delivery are normal (Refund policy 3.1).

entries.q: Why are the leaf tips turning brown?
entries.a: Brown tips usually come from uneven watering, cold air blowing straight from an AC vent, or salt build-up from fertiliser or tap water. Keep watering steady, move the plant out of direct AC airflow, flush the soil with plenty of water now and then, and trim the brown tips.
entries.original_a: Brown tips usually come from dry air, such as constant air conditioning, or uneven watering. Keep watering consistent, trim the tips, and avoid placing the plant directly in the AC airflow.
entries.note: Baseline indoor-ac: UAE AC rooms are not reliably dry (Sharjah study: about 61% RH). Cold AC draughts and uneven watering are the common causes.

entries.q: Why is my plant drooping?
entries.a: Drooping can mean thirst or overwatering. Check the soil: if dry, water well; if wet, hold off and check drainage. Moving a plant to a new spot can also cause temporary drooping.
entries.note: No conflict.

entries.q: My plant is dropping leaves after arrival. Should I worry?
entries.a: Some leaf drop is normal as a plant adjusts to new light and temperature, especially Fiddle Leaf Fig. Keep it in one spot, avoid frequent moves, and keep watering steady.
entries.note: Matches Refund policy 3.1 (adjustment leaf drop is normal).

entries.q: Do I need to repot my plant when it arrives?
entries.a: Not immediately. Let it settle for a few weeks first, and note that a repotted plant can't be returned or replaced, so check it's healthy before you repot. Plants in decorative pots arrive fully potted. Repot only when roots fill the pot or growth stops.
entries.original_a: Not immediately. Let it settle for a few weeks. Plants in decorative pots arrive fully potted. Repot only when roots fill the pot or growth stops.
entries.note: Refund policy 3.2 and 6: repotted plants cannot be returned or replaced, so customers should not repot until they are sure.

entries.q: I see tiny flying insects around my plant.
entries.a: These are often fungus gnats, caused by constantly damp soil. Let the soil dry between waterings and avoid leaving water in the saucer. If they persist, send a photo and our team will advise.
entries.note: No conflict.

entries.q: Which plants are easiest for beginners?
entries.a: Snake Plant, ZZ Plant and Golden Pothos are very forgiving. They handle low light and occasional missed waterings well.
entries.note: All three are in the catalog.

entries.q: Which plants are safe for cats and dogs?
entries.a: Areca Palm, Money Tree (Pachira) and Chinese Money Plant are generally considered non-toxic to cats and dogs. Even safe plants can upset a pet's stomach if chewed, so supervise curious pets.
entries.note: ASPCA lists areca palm and Pachira aquatica as non-toxic; Pilea peperomioides is not listed by name but related Pilea are non-toxic.

entries.q: Which plants are toxic to pets?
entries.a: Snake Plant, Peace Lily, ZZ Plant, Pothos, Rubber Plant and Fiddle Leaf Fig can irritate pets if chewed. Keep them out of reach, or choose pet-friendly options such as Areca Palm.
entries.note: Snake plant, peace lily, pothos, rubber plant and fiddle leaf fig are on ASPCA's toxic list; ZZ contains calcium oxalate.

entries.q: My pet chewed my plant. What should I do?
entries.a: Please contact your vet or a 24-hour animal emergency clinic right away and tell them the plant name. Don't wait for symptoms.
entries.note: No conflict.

entries.q: Which plants can I keep on a balcony in summer?
entries.a: UAE summer sun is intense, and many indoor plants burn outdoors. Choose plants from our Outdoor category for balconies, and keep indoor plants away from direct midday sun.
entries.note: Matches baseline summer-heat.

entries.q: Do plants really purify the air?
entries.a: Not noticeably in a normal room. Lab studies were done in small sealed chambers; a home would need far more plants than anyone keeps to match ordinary ventilation. Plants are great for greenery and wellbeing, but they don't replace ventilation or an air purifier.
entries.original_a: Plants can modestly support a fresher indoor feel, but they don't replace ventilation or air filtration. We recommend them mainly for greenery and wellbeing.
entries.note: Cummings & Waring 2019: 10–1,000 plants per m² would be needed to match normal ventilation. 'Modestly support a fresher indoor feel' overstates it; matches the Snake Plant guide now.

entries.q: What plants work in an office with no window?
entries.a: Low-light plants such as ZZ Plant, Snake Plant and Golden Pothos cope best. In a windowless room, bright artificial light still helps, and growth will be slow.
entries.note: Matches Snake Plant guide research (c22).

entries.q: Do I need plant food?
entries.a: Plants benefit from feeding in their growing season, roughly March to October in the UAE. Follow the label for dosage and don't feed a stressed or newly delivered plant.
